event: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland formally came into being.
facts: The union merged the parliaments of Great Britain and Ireland into one at Westminster.
A new Union Flag combined the crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick.
The change took effect at the very start of the new century's first year.

event: Revolutionary forces led by Fidel Castro took power in Cuba as the previous government fled.
facts: The takeover followed a guerrilla campaign waged largely from the Sierra Maestra mountains.
The capital, Havana, changed hands in the opening days of the year.
It reshaped Cuba's relationship with much of the wider world for decades.

event: Martin Luther was excommunicated by a papal decree for refusing to recant his writings.
facts: The dispute began with his objections to the sale of indulgences.
His ideas spread quickly thanks to the recently invented printing press.
The break helped launch the Protestant Reformation across Europe.

event: Isaac Newton, who would formulate the laws of motion and universal gravitation, was born.
facts: He later served as Master of the Royal Mint, pursuing counterfeiters.
His major work, the Principia, laid out three laws of motion.
He also made foundational contributions to the study of light and optics.

event: Joan of Arc, the French heroine of the Hundred Years' War, was born in Domremy.
facts: She helped lift the siege of Orleans while still a teenager.
She was later canonized as a saint, centuries after her death.
Her village lay on the frontier between French and Burgundian lands.

event: Galileo Galilei first observed the four largest moons of Jupiter through his telescope.
facts: These bodies are now called the Galilean moons in his honor.
Their orbits showed that not everything circled the Earth.
He recorded the moons as small 'stars' shifting night to night.

event: Galileo Galilei, pioneering astronomer and physicist, died near Florence.
facts: He spent his final years under house arrest after a famous trial.
He improved the telescope and turned it toward the night sky.
His studies of falling bodies foreshadowed later laws of motion.

event: Civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia.
facts: He became a leading voice for nonviolent protest.
He delivered a celebrated speech at a march in the nation's capital.
A national holiday in the United States now honors his birthday.

event: Benjamin Franklin, statesman, printer and inventor, was born in Boston.
facts: He famously experimented with electricity and lightning.
He helped draft and sign the founding documents of the United States.
He founded one of the first public lending libraries in the colonies.

event: England's first elected parliament to include commoners met in Westminster.
facts: It was summoned during a baronial revolt against the king.
Representatives came from both towns and shires.
It marked an early step toward representative government.

event: Gold was discovered at a sawmill in California, sparking a vast migration west.
facts: The find at the mill set off the California Gold Rush.
Prospectors who arrived the next year were nicknamed 'forty-niners'.
The rush rapidly swelled California's population and economy.

event: The poet Robert Burns, Scotland's national bard, was born in Alloway.
facts: His birthday is celebrated each year with a 'Burns supper'.
He wrote in both Scots and English.
He penned the song traditionally sung at the new year.

event: Composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg.
facts: He began composing as a small child and toured Europe young.
He wrote symphonies, operas and concertos in great number.
He completed hundreds of works in a life of only thirty-five years.

event: The Auschwitz concentration camp was liberated by advancing Soviet troops.
facts: The date is now marked as an international day of remembrance.
It was the largest of the Nazi camp complexes.
Survivors and historians work to preserve its memory as a warning.

event: Henry VIII of England died, ending a reign of nearly thirty-eight years.
facts: His break with Rome led to the Church of England.
He was succeeded by his young son Edward VI.
He had six wives over the course of his life.

event: King Charles I of England was executed following his defeat in the civil war.
facts: England briefly became a republic afterward, called the Commonwealth.
He was tried for high treason by a special court.
The monarchy was restored just over a decade later.

event: James Joyce's landmark novel 'Ulysses' was published in Paris.
facts: Its events unfold over a single day in Dublin.
The book was published on the author's birthday.
It is famous for its experimental, stream-of-consciousness style.

event: George Washington was unanimously chosen as the first U.S. president by the electors.
facts: He had led the Continental Army during the Revolution.
He set the precedent of stepping down after two terms.
He presided over the convention that drafted the Constitution.

event: The Treaty of Waitangi was first signed between the British Crown and Maori chiefs.
facts: It is regarded as a founding document of New Zealand.
The day is now a national holiday there.
Different language versions of the text have long been debated.

event: The novelist Charles Dickens was born in Portsmouth, England.
facts: He gave hugely popular public readings of his own work.
Many of his novels first appeared in monthly installments.
He drew on his own hard childhood in several stories.

event: Mary, Queen of Scots, was executed at Fotheringhay Castle in England.
facts: She had spent many years in captivity before her death.
Her son later became king of both Scotland and England.
She was implicated in plots against her cousin, the English queen.

event: Henry VIII was recognized as supreme head of the Church of England by the clergy.
facts: The move followed his dispute with the pope over his marriage.
It transferred church authority in England to the crown.
It set the stage for the dissolution of the monasteries.

event: Abraham Lincoln and Charles Darwin were both born on this same day.
facts: Lincoln would lead the United States through its civil war.
Darwin would propose the theory of evolution by natural selection.
The coincidence of their shared birthday is often noted.

event: A notorious gangland shooting took place in Chicago, later widely dramatized.
facts: It occurred during the era of nationwide alcohol prohibition.
Rival bootlegging gangs were competing for control.
The event became a symbol of Prohibition-era crime.

event: The astronomer and physicist Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa.
facts: He is sometimes called the father of modern observational astronomy.
He championed the idea that the Earth orbits the Sun.
He studied motion by rolling balls down inclined planes.

event: The astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus was born in Torun, in present-day Poland.
facts: He argued that the Sun, not the Earth, sat at the center.
His great book appeared only as he was dying.
His model reshaped how people pictured the heavens.

event: A short, influential political pamphlet by Marx and Engels was first published in London.
facts: It called for workers across nations to unite.
It appeared during a year of revolutions across Europe.
It became one of the most widely read political texts.

event: George Washington, the first U.S. president, was born in colonial Virginia.
facts: He commanded American forces during the Revolutionary War.
The capital city of the United States is named for him.
He declined to become a king after the war.

event: The Gutenberg Bible, an early book printed with movable type, is traditionally dated.
facts: It was produced in Mainz, in present-day Germany.
Printing made books far cheaper and more plentiful.
Only a few dozen copies are known to survive today.

event: Napoleon Bonaparte escaped from exile on the island of Elba.
facts: His return began a period known as the Hundred Days.
He had been sent to Elba after his first abdication.
His final defeat came months later at Waterloo.

event: The first session of the United States Congress convened in New York City.
facts: It put the new federal Constitution into practice.
The body was divided into a Senate and a House.
New York briefly served as the nation's capital.

event: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died after decades in power.
facts: His death set off a struggle over who would succeed him.
He had led the Soviet Union through the Second World War.
His rule was marked by sweeping and often brutal campaigns.

event: The artist Michelangelo Buonarroti was born in Tuscany.
facts: He sculpted the famous statue of David.
He painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
He also worked as an architect and a poet.

event: A Portuguese fleet under Pedro Alvares Cabral set sail and later reached Brazil.
facts: The voyage was officially bound for India.
It claimed the Brazilian coast for Portugal.
The expedition rounded much of the Atlantic on its way.

event: Mohandas Gandhi began the Salt March, a long protest walk to the sea.
facts: It defied a tax and monopoly on salt.
Marchers walked roughly 240 miles to the coast.
It became a landmark of nonviolent resistance.

event: The physicist Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, in present-day Germany.
facts: He developed the theory of relativity.
He won a Nobel Prize for work on the photoelectric effect.
His equation linking mass and energy is widely known.

event: The Roman dictator Julius Caesar was assassinated in the Senate.
facts: The date was known to Romans as the Ides of March.
His death plunged Rome into renewed civil war.
His heir later became the first Roman emperor.

event: Saint Patrick, the patron saint associated with Ireland, is traditionally said to have died.
facts: He is credited with spreading Christianity in Ireland.
He was not Irish by birth but came from Roman Britain.
His feast day is now celebrated around the world.

event: Isaac Newton, one of the most influential scientists in history, died in London.
facts: He was buried in Westminster Abbey.
He had served as president of the Royal Society.
He laid the mathematical foundations of classical physics.

event: The composer Johann Sebastian Bach was born in Eisenach, in present-day Germany.
facts: He came from a large and very musical family.
He wrote extensively for organ and for choirs.
Much of his fame grew long after his death.

event: The expression 'OK' is widely traced to a newspaper appearance around this time.
facts: It is now one of the most recognized words worldwide.
Its exact origins were long debated by language scholars.
It spread rapidly through telegraph and print.

event: Queen Elizabeth I of England died, ending the Tudor dynasty.
facts: Her long reign is often called a golden age.
She never married and had no direct heir.
The Scottish king succeeded her, uniting the crowns.

event: The painter Vincent van Gogh was born in the Netherlands.
facts: He sold very few paintings during his lifetime.
He produced hundreds of works in just a decade.
His bold color and brushwork influenced modern art.

event: The Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de Leon first sighted the coast of Florida.
facts: He is said to have named the land for a Spanish feast of flowers.
He was searching, by legend, for renewal and riches.
His landing was among the first European visits to the region.

event: Civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee.
facts: He had traveled there to support striking sanitation workers.
His death prompted national mourning and unrest.
He had won the Nobel Peace Prize a few years earlier.

event: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece.
facts: They revived an ancient festival held in Olympia.
Athletes from over a dozen nations took part.
The marathon race honored a legend from ancient Greece.

event: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered, effectively ending the American Civil War.
facts: The surrender took place at Appomattox Court House.
The war had lasted four years and cost enormous casualties.
It cleared the way for reunification of the country.

event: The American Civil War began with the bombardment of Fort Sumter.
facts: The fort guarded the harbor of Charleston, South Carolina.
No soldiers were killed in the opening exchange.
The conflict would last four years.

event: Yuri Gagarin became the first human to travel into outer space.
facts: He completed a single orbit of the Earth.
His flight lasted under two hours.
He returned safely and became world-famous.

event: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln was shot at a theater in Washington and died the next day.
facts: The attack came days after the Civil War effectively ended.
He was attending a play that evening.
His death stunned a nation just beginning to heal.

event: The artist and inventor Leonardo da Vinci was born near Vinci, in Tuscany.
facts: He painted the Mona Lisa and the Last Supper.
His notebooks brim with inventions and anatomical studies.
He wrote many notes in a distinctive mirror script.

event: The ocean liner Titanic sank in the North Atlantic after striking an iceberg.
facts: It was on its very first voyage at the time.
There were too few lifeboats for everyone aboard.
The disaster led to new rules for safety at sea.

event: A powerful earthquake and fire devastated San Francisco.
facts: Much of the city was destroyed in the days that followed.
Fires raged as water mains broke.
The disaster reshaped how cities prepared for earthquakes.

event: The first battles of the American Revolutionary War were fought at Lexington and Concord.
facts: They are remembered for 'the shot heard round the world'.
Colonial militias confronted British regulars.
The clashes turned a political crisis into open war.

event: Rome was, by tradition, founded on this day.
facts: The legend credits the twin brothers Romulus and Remus.
The date long anchored the Roman calendar of years.
The city would grow into a vast Mediterranean empire.

event: The playwright William Shakespeare is traditionally said to have been born in Stratford.
facts: He is also traditionally said to have died on the same date years later.
He wrote comedies, tragedies and histories.
His plays are still performed all over the world.

event: A landmark scientific paper describing the structure of DNA was published.
facts: It proposed the now-famous double helix shape.
The work drew on X-ray images of the molecule.
It opened the way to modern molecular biology.

event: George Washington took the oath of office as the first U.S. president.
facts: The ceremony took place in New York City.
He wore a plain American-made suit for the occasion.
He had been chosen unanimously by the electors.

event: The Empire State Building opened in New York City.
facts: It was the tallest building in the world at the time.
It was built in only about a year.
Its observation decks quickly became a tourist draw.

event: Rhode Island declared its independence from Britain ahead of the other colonies.
facts: It was the smallest of the original thirteen colonies.
The move came weeks before the broader Declaration.
It reflected strong local resentment of British rule.

event: The political philosopher Karl Marx was born in Trier, in present-day Germany.
facts: He co-wrote an influential political pamphlet.
He spent much of his later life in London.
He wrote a major work analyzing capitalism.

event: The Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp, went into use in Britain.
facts: It carried a profile of the young queen.
It made prepaid postage simple and cheap.
Collectors prize surviving examples today.

event: Victory in Europe was celebrated as Nazi Germany's surrender took effect.
facts: Crowds filled the streets of many Allied cities.
The war in the Pacific continued for months more.
The day is remembered as V-E Day.

event: The city of Constantinople was formally dedicated as a new imperial capital.
facts: It was built on the site of the older town of Byzantium.
It guarded a vital strait between two seas.
It served as a capital for over a thousand years.

event: Edward Jenner carried out an early test of vaccination against smallpox.
facts: He used material from the milder cowpox disease.
The word 'vaccine' comes from the Latin for cow.
His work helped lead to the eventual eradication of smallpox.

event: The explorer Christopher Columbus died in Valladolid, Spain.
facts: He had made four voyages across the Atlantic.
He believed he had reached the edge of Asia.
He died without fully knowing the scale of his discoveries.

event: The American Red Cross was founded by Clara Barton.
facts: Barton had nursed soldiers during the Civil War.
The group provides disaster and emergency relief.
It became part of a wider international movement.

event: Samuel Morse sent a famous message over an experimental telegraph line.
facts: The line ran between Washington and Baltimore.
The message read, 'What hath God wrought'.
The telegraph soon shrank distances for communication.

event: The first 'Star Wars' film opened in theaters in the United States.
facts: It became a cultural phenomenon almost overnight.
Its special effects pushed the craft forward.
It launched one of the most successful film series ever.

event: The city of Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Empire after a long siege.
facts: The event is often used to mark the end of the medieval era.
Heavy cannon helped breach the city's ancient walls.
The city became the Ottoman capital.

event: Climbers Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest.
facts: It was the first confirmed ascent of the world's highest peak.
News reached the wider world days later.
Their feat made headlines around the globe.

event: The Montgolfier brothers publicly demonstrated a hot-air balloon in France.
facts: The unmanned balloon rose high into the air.
Later that year a balloon carried human passengers.
It opened the age of human flight.

event: Allied forces landed in Normandy on D-Day during the Second World War.
facts: It was one of the largest seaborne invasions in history.
The landings opened a major front against Nazi Germany.
Several beaches were assaulted at once along the coast.

event: The Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, died in Medina.
facts: He had united much of the Arabian Peninsula.
His teachings are recorded in the Quran.
His death led to the early caliphates.

event: The Continental Congress adopted the Stars and Stripes as the U.S. flag.
facts: The design featured thirteen stars and stripes.
Stars were later added as new states joined.
The day is now marked as Flag Day.

event: King John of England sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede.
facts: It limited the power of the crown by law.
It was forced on the king by rebellious barons.
It influenced later ideas of constitutional rights.

event: Napoleon Bonaparte was decisively defeated at the Battle of Waterloo.
facts: The battle took place in present-day Belgium.
Allied and Prussian armies combined against him.
It ended his final bid to rule France.

event: Enslaved people in Texas were informed of their freedom, an event marked as Juneteenth.
facts: News came more than two years after emancipation was proclaimed.
The day is now a federal holiday in the United States.
It is celebrated with community gatherings and reflection.

event: New Hampshire ratified the U.S. Constitution, the ninth state to do so.
facts: Nine states were needed to put it into effect.
Its vote thus brought the Constitution into force.
The remaining states ratified over the following years.

event: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand helped trigger the First World War.
facts: It took place in the city of Sarajevo.
A chain of alliances drew many nations into war.
The conflict would last more than four years.

event: The Treaty of Versailles was signed, formally ending the First World War.
facts: It was signed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
It imposed heavy terms on Germany.
It established the League of Nations.

event: Several British North American colonies united to form the Dominion of Canada.
facts: The day is now celebrated as Canada Day.
It joined provinces under one federal government.
More provinces and territories joined later.

event: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence.
facts: It announced the colonies' separation from Britain.
Its date is celebrated as American Independence Day.
Its words on liberty have inspired movements worldwide.

event: A Paris crowd stormed the Bastille fortress, igniting the French Revolution.
facts: The fortress was a symbol of royal authority.
The day is now France's national holiday.
Few prisoners were actually held there at the time.

event: Apollo 11 launched from Florida on its way to the first crewed Moon landing.
facts: Three astronauts rode atop a giant rocket.
The journey to the Moon took several days.
Millions watched the launch on television.

event: Apollo 11 astronauts became the first humans to walk on the Moon.
facts: The first bootprints were left in the lunar dust.
A famous line marked the moment for humankind.
Hundreds of millions watched or listened worldwide.

event: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, a wonder of the ancient world, was destroyed by fire.
facts: It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
It was later rebuilt before falling into ruin.
Its remains lie in present-day Turkey.

event: Austria-Hungary declared war, marking a formal start of the First World War.
facts: The declaration followed a royal assassination.
Alliances quickly pulled other powers into the war.
Much of Europe mobilized within days.

event: Joseph Priestley isolated oxygen gas in a famous experiment.
facts: He heated a compound and collected the gas released.
Others soon helped explain its role in burning.
The discovery reshaped the new science of chemistry.

event: An atomic bomb was dropped on the Japanese city of Hiroshima.
facts: It was the first use of such a weapon in war.
A second bomb fell on Nagasaki days later.
Japan surrendered shortly afterward, ending the war.

event: A treaty fixed much of the border between the United States and British Canada.
facts: It settled long-running disputes in the northeast.
It helped keep the peace between the two nations.
Negotiators are remembered in the treaty's name.

event: Japan's surrender was announced, effectively ending the Second World War.
facts: The news set off celebrations in many countries.
Formal surrender documents were signed weeks later.
The day is remembered as V-J Day.

event: Napoleon Bonaparte was born on the island of Corsica.
facts: He rose from soldier to emperor of the French.
He reformed law with a famous legal code.
He was eventually exiled to a remote island.

event: India became independent from British rule.
facts: The territory was partitioned into two nations.
Millions were displaced in the months that followed.
Independence Day is now a national holiday in India.

event: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius buried the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
facts: Ash preserved many buildings and objects for centuries.
An eyewitness left a famous written account.
The buried towns were rediscovered much later.

event: France's National Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
facts: It proclaimed liberty and equality before the law.
It became a key text of the French Revolution.
Its ideas spread far beyond France.

event: Hundreds of thousands gathered in Washington for a march for civil rights.
facts: Martin Luther King Jr. delivered a celebrated speech there.
Demonstrators called for jobs and freedom.
It helped build support for new civil rights laws.

event: A great fire broke out in London and burned for several days.
facts: It destroyed much of the medieval walled city.
It began in a bakery on Pudding Lane.
Rebuilding led to new brick-and-stone construction.

event: Japan formally signed surrender documents aboard a warship in Tokyo Bay.
facts: The ceremony marked the official end of World War II.
Allied representatives gathered for the signing.
The war had lasted six years across the globe.

event: The Continental Congress officially named the new nation the United States of America.
facts: The name replaced the older 'United Colonies'.
It came soon after the Declaration of Independence.
The choice reflected a union of independent states.

event: Francis Scott Key wrote the poem that became the U.S. national anthem.
facts: He watched a fort withstand a night of bombardment.
The words were set to an existing tune.
It officially became the anthem more than a century later.

event: Delegates signed the United States Constitution in Philadelphia.
facts: It created a framework for the federal government.
It still functions as the nation's supreme law.
A bill of rights was added soon afterward.

event: President Lincoln issued a preliminary proclamation to free enslaved people.
facts: It applied to areas in rebellion against the Union.
The final proclamation took effect the next year.
It reframed the aims of the Civil War.

event: Francis Drake completed a voyage circumnavigating the globe.
facts: His was the second expedition to sail all the way around.
He returned laden with treasure.
He was later knighted for the feat.

event: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite.
facts: Its radio beeps could be heard around the world.
It opened the era of the space race.
It was about the size of a beach ball.

event: Christopher Columbus's expedition reached islands in the Caribbean.
facts: He had sailed west hoping to reach Asia.
The landfall opened lasting contact between continents.
His ships had been at sea for many weeks.

event: The Norman army defeated the English at the Battle of Hastings.
facts: The victory led to the Norman conquest of England.
The English king was killed in the fighting.
The campaign is depicted in a famous embroidery.

event: A British fleet won the naval Battle of Trafalgar against France and Spain.
facts: The British admiral was killed during the battle.
It secured British control of the seas for years.
A famous London square is named for the battle.

event: A dramatic stock market crash began on Wall Street.
facts: The collapse helped usher in the Great Depression.
Panic selling spread over several days.
It wiped out fortunes large and small.

event: The explorer and writer Walter Raleigh was executed in London.
facts: He had helped popularize tobacco in England.
He led expeditions to the Americas.
He wrote a sweeping history during his imprisonment.

event: Martin Luther is said to have posted his Ninety-Five Theses on a church door.
facts: The act challenged the sale of indulgences.
It is often used to date the Reformation's start.
The site was in Wittenberg, in present-day Germany.

event: The Berlin Wall was opened, allowing free passage between East and West.
facts: Crowds celebrated atop the wall that night.
It had divided the city for nearly three decades.
Its fall hastened the end of the Cold War.

event: An armistice ended the fighting of the First World War.
facts: It took effect at the eleventh hour of the day.
The day is now marked for remembrance.
Millions had died over four years of war.

event: President Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at a battlefield cemetery.
facts: The speech was famously brief.
It honored soldiers who had died there.
It restated the nation's founding ideals.

event: U.S. President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas, Texas.
facts: He was riding in an open car through the city.
The vice president was sworn in hours later.
The event shocked people around the world.

event: Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species'.
facts: It set out the theory of evolution by natural selection.
The first printing sold out quickly.
It transformed the study of living things.

event: The British statesman Winston Churchill was born.
facts: He led Britain through much of the Second World War.
He was also a prolific writer and historian.
He won a Nobel Prize in Literature.

event: Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama.
facts: Her arrest sparked a long bus boycott.
The boycott helped launch the civil rights movement.
She became an enduring symbol of quiet resistance.

event: A surprise attack on Pearl Harbor brought the United States into World War II.
facts: The naval base lay in Hawaii.
The U.S. declared war the following day.
The date was called one that would live in infamy.

event: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded, on the anniversary of the founder's death.
facts: They honored work in several fields of achievement.
The prizes were funded by an inventor's fortune.
They remain among the world's most prestigious awards.

event: The Bill of Rights was ratified, adding ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution.
facts: It protected freedoms such as speech and religion.
It addressed concerns raised during ratification.
It remains central to American law.

event: Colonists threw chests of tea into Boston Harbor in protest.
facts: The act protested taxes imposed from afar.
It became known as the Boston Tea Party.
It helped push the colonies toward revolution.

event: The Wright brothers made the first powered, controlled airplane flights.
facts: The flights took place at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
The longest of the day lasted under a minute.
Their machine had been built and tested by hand.

event: The Pilgrims aboard the Mayflower are traditionally said to have landed at Plymouth.
facts: They had crossed the Atlantic seeking a new home.
Their first winter was harsh and deadly.
They later shared a harvest feast remembered as Thanksgiving.

event: The earliest recorded celebration of Christmas on December 25 is traditionally dated to Rome.
facts: The date was fixed centuries after the events it marks.
It later became one of the most widely observed holidays.
Customs around it vary greatly across cultures.

event: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.
facts: The coronation revived an imperial title in the west.
He ruled a vast realm across western Europe.
His reign spurred a revival of learning.

event: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was formally established.
facts: It united several republics under one government.
It would last for nearly seven decades.
It became a leading power of the twentieth century.

event: The fall of Granada ended centuries of Muslim rule in the Iberian Peninsula.
facts: It completed the long Christian reconquest of Spain.
It happened the same year as Columbus's first voyage.
The Alhambra palace passed to Spanish rule.

event: Edward the Confessor, king of England, died, setting off a disputed succession.
facts: His death led to rival claims to the throne.
One claim ended at the Battle of Hastings that year.
He had founded a great abbey at Westminster.

event: The trial of Joan of Arc began in occupied France.
facts: She faced charges before a church court.
She had led French troops to several victories.
She was later declared innocent and a saint.

event: Alexander Hamilton, a founding figure of the United States, was born in the Caribbean.
facts: He became the first U.S. Treasury Secretary.
He helped design the new nation's finances.
He co-wrote influential essays defending the Constitution.

event: The first public museum in the American colonies opened in Charleston.
facts: It gathered natural history specimens for display.
Public museums were a new idea at the time.
It survives as one of the country's oldest.

event: The explorer James Cook became one of the first Europeans to reach the Hawaiian Islands.
facts: He named them after a British patron.
He had charted much of the Pacific.
His voyages greatly expanded European maps.

event: King Louis XVI of France was executed during the French Revolution.
facts: The monarchy had already been abolished.
His death deepened divisions across Europe.
His wife was executed later that year.

event: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom died after a reign of more than 63 years.
facts: Her reign gave its name to the Victorian era.
She presided over a vast empire.
She was succeeded by her son Edward VII.

event: A British fleet established the first European settlement at Sydney, Australia.
facts: The day is now marked as Australia Day.
The fleet had sailed from England months before.
It founded a penal colony at first.

event: The poem 'The Raven' by Edgar Allan Poe was first published.
facts: It brought the author wide fame.
Its haunting refrain became famous.
Poe helped shape the modern short story.

event: President Lincoln signed the resolution proposing the amendment to abolish slavery.
facts: The amendment was later ratified by the states.
It permanently ended legal slavery in the country.
It was the thirteenth amendment to the Constitution.

event: Johannes Gutenberg, who helped introduce printing with movable type in Europe, died.
facts: His press transformed how knowledge spread.
He printed an early edition of the Bible.
He worked in the city of Mainz.

event: Queen Victoria married Prince Albert in London.
facts: Her white wedding gown set a lasting fashion.
The couple had nine children.
Albert promoted science, art and industry.

event: The artist Michelangelo died in Rome at nearly ninety years old.
facts: He had worked into his final days.
He shaped the art of the Renaissance.
His designs influenced the dome of St Peter's.

event: A papal decree introduced the Gregorian calendar reform.
facts: It corrected drift in the older Julian calendar.
Some countries adopted it only much later.
It is the calendar most of the world uses today.

event: An early organized Mardi Gras celebration is recorded in New Orleans.
facts: The festival features parades and masked revelers.

He worked on it for years on scaffolding.
It is among the most admired artworks ever.

event: A major public television broadcasting service began regular programming.
facts: It was among the earliest such services.
Few homes had sets at the time.
Television would soon transform daily life.

event: An animal named Laika became the first living creature to orbit the Earth.
facts: She traveled aboard a Soviet satellite.
The mission tested survival in space.
It paved the way for human flight.

event: The entrance to the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun was found in Egypt.
facts: The tomb held dazzling treasures.
It had lain largely undisturbed for ages.
The find made headlines worldwide.

event: A plot to blow up England's Parliament was foiled.
facts: The day is still marked with bonfires.
A conspirator was caught guarding the gunpowder.
It became a famous moment in British memory.

event: Abraham Lincoln was elected president of the United States.
facts: His election deepened sectional tensions.
Several states soon moved to secede.
Civil war followed within months.

event: The scientist Marie Curie was born in Warsaw.
facts: She conducted pioneering work on radioactivity.
She won Nobel Prizes in two sciences.
She was the first woman to win the prize.

event: Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays.
facts: He noticed an unknown form of radiation.
It could reveal bones inside the body.
It quickly transformed medicine.

event: An explorer found the long-sought missionary David Livingstone in Africa.
facts: A famous greeting is associated with the meeting.
Livingstone had been out of contact for years.
The search had drawn wide public interest.

event: King Canute, ruler of England and much of Scandinavia, died.
facts: He is linked to a famous tale about the tide.
His empire spanned the North Sea.
It broke apart after his death.

event: An early helicopter briefly lifted off the ground in France.
facts: It was among the first such flights.
Vertical flight proved difficult to master.
Decades passed before practical machines flew.

event: The novel 'Moby-Dick' was published in the United States.
facts: It tells of a hunt for a great white whale.
It found wide acclaim only later.
It is now considered a classic.

event: A Union army began its march through Georgia in the American Civil War.
facts: It aimed to break the South's will to fight.
It cut a wide path to the sea.
It became a famous campaign of the war.

event: A small Spanish force captured the Inca ruler at Cajamarca.
facts: It led to the fall of the Inca Empire.
The empire had stretched along the Andes.
It changed the history of South America.

event: The Suez Canal opened, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
facts: It shortened the sea route to Asia.
It took years to dig.
It became a vital waterway for trade.

event: A famous animated cartoon character made his sound-film debut.
facts: The short was an early talking cartoon.
It helped launch a major studio.
The character became known worldwide.

event: New Jersey became the first state to ratify the U.S. Bill of Rights.
facts: The amendments protected basic freedoms.
Other states followed over the next two years.
It strengthened the new Constitution.

event: The first untethered human flight in a hot-air balloon took place over Paris.
facts: Two men rode above the city.
Crowds watched in amazement.
It opened the age of human flight.

event: A famous weekly photo magazine published its first issue.
facts: It told stories largely through pictures.
It shaped photojournalism for decades.
Its images captured major events.

event: The inventor Alfred Nobel patented dynamite.
facts: It made blasting safer and more controllable.
His later will funded the Nobel Prizes.
He held many patents in his lifetime.

event: The first national Thanksgiving was observed in the United States by proclamation.
facts: The first president had called for the day.
It gave thanks for the new nation.
It became an annual tradition over time.

event: Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade at a council in France.
facts: His appeal drew a large response.
Armies set out toward the east.
It began centuries of crusading.

event: The Royal Society, a famous scientific body, held a founding meeting in London.
facts: It promoted experiment and observation.
It published an early scientific journal.
It counted many great scientists as members.

event: A plan to partition a Middle Eastern territory was approved by the United Nations.
facts: It aimed to create two states.
It set the stage for major change in the region.
Its consequences are still felt today.

event: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in Paris.
facts: The ceremony took place in a great cathedral.
He reportedly took the crown into his own hands.
It marked the height of his power.

event: The first human-to-human heart transplant was performed in South Africa.
facts: A surgical team carried out the operation.
It was a landmark in medicine.
It opened the way for future transplants.

event: A famous London newspaper, The Observer, published its first edition.
facts: It is among the oldest Sunday papers.
It reported on news and society.
It is still published today.

event: Christopher Columbus reached the island of Hispaniola.
facts: It is shared today by two nations.
He established an early settlement there.
It became a base for further exploration.

event: An early edition of the Encyclopaedia Britannica appeared.
facts: It gathered knowledge into reference volumes.
It was produced in Scotland.
It became a famous reference work.

event: An actress is recorded appearing on the English public stage, a notable first.
facts: Women's roles had long been played by boys.
The change followed the reopening of theaters.
It transformed English drama.

event: An early daily newspaper began publication in New York.
facts: The press was spreading rapidly.
Papers shaped public debate.
Cities competed for readers.

event: Indiana was admitted as a U.S. state.
facts: It became the nineteenth state.
Settlers had moved into the territory.
Its name reflects its early peoples.

event: The first transatlantic radio signal was received by Guglielmo Marconi.
facts: It crossed the ocean without wires.
It proved long-distance wireless was possible.
It opened the age of radio.

event: Francis Drake set sail on the voyage that would circle the globe.
facts: He left from an English port.
He returned laden with treasure.
He was the second to sail around the world.

event: Roald Amundsen's team became the first to reach the South Pole.
facts: They beat a rival British expedition.
They traveled by ski and dog sled.
They returned safely to their base.

event: The amendment abolishing slavery was declared ratified in the United States.
facts: It ended slavery throughout the nation.
It was the thirteenth amendment.
It marked a turning point in history.

event: Charles Dickens published 'A Christmas Carol'.
facts: It tells of a miser's transformation.
It helped shape modern Christmas customs.
It has been adapted countless times.

event: The vast Louisiana Territory was formally transferred to the United States.
facts: It roughly doubled the nation's size.
It had been purchased from France.
It opened a huge region to settlement.

event: Beethoven's Fifth and Sixth Symphonies premiered together in Vienna.
facts: The concert was very long and cold.
Both works became enduring favorites.
The Fifth opens with a famous motif.

event: The painter Vincent van Gogh suffered a famous crisis in Arles, France.
facts: He continued to paint prolifically.
He created some of his greatest works there.
His letters describe his struggles.

event: A treaty signed at Ghent ended the war between Britain and the United States.
facts: News traveled slowly across the ocean.
A major battle was fought before word arrived.
It restored peace between the nations.

event: Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of radium.
facts: It was a new radioactive element.
Their work won wide acclaim.
It advanced the study of radioactivity.

event: Charles Darwin set sail aboard the Beagle on his famous voyage.
facts: The journey lasted nearly five years.
His observations shaped his later theory.
He studied wildlife on distant shores.

event: The first public film screening for a paying audience was held in Paris.
facts: Short moving pictures amazed viewers.
It helped launch the film industry.
The brothers behind it became famous.

event: The archbishop Thomas Becket was killed in Canterbury Cathedral.
facts: He had clashed with the king.
He was later declared a saint.
His shrine drew many pilgrims.

event: A famous brewery was founded in Dublin under a long lease.
facts: Its founder signed a nine-thousand-year lease.
Its dark stout became known worldwide.
It grew into a major export.
